(See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Fixes a crash on the form builder's edit page when the form has no encounter type. The Audit Details tab read `form.encounterType.uuid` without a null check. Encounter type is optional on OpenMRS forms (core's `FormValidator` only requires a name and version), so the REST API returns `encounterType: null` for forms created without one. The framework's error boundary catches the resulting TypeError, but it wraps the whole form builder app, so the entire edit page gets replaced with "An error has occurred. Please try reloading the page." I reproduced this locally and on dev3. The Encounter Type row now shows "None" for these forms. I've also guarded the `changedBy` read in the Last Edited By row so it falls back to "Unknown", the same way Created By already handles a missing creator. The form builder's save modal requires an encounter type, so forms without one come from REST or other clients. ## Screenshots Before: After: ## Related Issue ## Other

## Summary
"Validate and publish form" and "Publish form" are now disabled until the form has a saved JSON schema.

Before, a form with no saved JSON schema could still be published. Publishing only marks the saved form as published, so the buttons check what's saved rather than what's in the editor. The editor can hold a schema that was never saved, from a restored browser draft, rendered changes, or the dummy schema. Validation also returns no errors for a missing schema, so "Validate and publish form" went straight on to publish the form. A form can end up without a schema if it was created outside the form builder, or if saving fails after its old schema resource is removed.

title: (chore) Share SWR through module federation
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Adds `swr` to `peerDependencies` so the build tooling federates it, and pins the exact `2.5.1` devDependency so the fallback copy matches the app shell.

The openmrs rspack config builds the module federation `shared` list from `peerDependencies`. `swr` was only reaching this app transitively, so the built entry registered no `swr` share and bundled a private copy. `useSWR` from that copy reads its own `SWRConfig` context, not the one the framework's component decorator provides, so the form builder has been running on SWR's stock defaults (revalidate on focus and reconnect, unlimited retries on every error) and its own cache rather than the shared one.

You can see the symptom on dev3 today: open the form builder, switch tabs and come back, and the forms list refetches. With this change it doesn't, because the framework's `revalidateOnFocus: false` now applies.

Verified by building and checking the remote entry, which now registers `swr`, `swr/_internal`, `swr/immutable` and `swr/infinite` at 2.5.1 like the other O3 apps, and by running the dev server against the dev3 backend and confirming the forms list no longer refetches on window focus.

The compressed-size action builds the pull request and base revisions sequentially in the same workspace. When the base build is restored from the Turborepo cache, its build command is skipped and stale pull-request chunks can remain in `dist`. Those files are then incorrectly reported as removed, inflating the bundle-size change.

This adds the action-supported cleanup hook and a package-owned `clean` script scoped to the ignored `dist` directory. Cleanup therefore runs independently of whether the subsequent build is executed or restored from cache.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

The "Search this list" field on the forms dashboard rendered taller than the adjacent "Create a new form" button, overflowing the toolbar and overlapping the table header row.

The search had no explicit `size`, so it fell back to Carbon's `TableToolbarSearch` default of `size="lg"` (48px), while the button is `size={responsiveSize}` (`sm` = 32px on desktop). `TableToolbarSearch` does not inherit size from the parent `<TableToolbar size=...>` — that only adds a class to the toolbar wrapper, and Carbon keys the small styling on the search's own `--search--sm` class. The two controls lined up only by coincidence with whatever Carbon version the app shell shipped; a newer Carbon singleton exposed the mismatch.

The fix passes `size={responsiveSize}` to the search so both controls share the same responsive size (`sm` on desktop, `lg` on tablet) regardless of the Carbon version in use.

## Screenshots

<!-- before/after -->

## Related Issue

## Other

Verified locally against a backend at `http://localhost`: the search bar and the "Create a new form" button are now equal height and the table header is no longer overlapped.

No test added: the only thing to assert would be that the search carries the `cds--search--sm` class, which is a brittle implementation-detail assertion. Verified visually instead.

## Summary

Migrates form-builder's test runner from jest to vitest, aligning it with the patterns adopted across the rest of the O3 apps.

Changes:
- Replace `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, and `@types/jest` with `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`, and `cross-env`. Bump `@testing-library/jest-dom` (6.4 → 6.8) so its `/vitest` subpath is available, and bump `@testing-library/dom` (9.x → 10.x) and `@testing-library/react` (14.x → 16.x) for the matching React 18+ / RTL 16 compatibility.
- Add `vitest.config.ts`: `jsdom` environment, `.scss`/`.css` aliased to `identity-obj-proxy` via the anchored `^.*\.s?css$` regex, `@openmrs/esm-framework` aliased to its mock, `react-i18next` and `react-markdown` aliased to their local `__mocks__` files, and the pre-existing `@resources`/`@hooks`/`@types`/`@tools`/`@constants` path shortcuts replicated as vitest aliases. Alias replacements are resolved with `fileURLToPath` (via a small `r()` helper) so they stay portable on Windows. `fakeTimers.toFake` is limited to the timers jsdom actually provides so it does not break React's scheduler.
- Update `tools/setup-tests.ts` to load `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` and swap `jest.fn` for `vi.fn` in the `window.URL.createObjectURL` mock. Testing-library auto-cleans up between tests when `afterEach` is globally available (it is, via vitest's `globals: true`), so the manual `cleanup` call from the jest setup is dropped.
- Convert the twenty test files to the vitest API: explicit imports for `describe`/`expect`/`it`/`vi` (plus `beforeEach`/`test`/`type Mock`/`type MockedFunction` where actually used), `jest.*` swapped for `vi.*`. - Pass an empty implementation function to `vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {})` calls; vitest's `mockImplementation` requires an argument where jest's was optional.
